summary: Compute the non-relativistic thermal-electron normalized momentum p_Te = sqrt(2T/mc^2). It is a dimensionless speed ratio v/c, not a velocity in cm/s, and must not be passed directly as vnorm to normalized-momentum. Intermediate overflow and final non-representability are handled separately, so a representable result is neither falsely rejected nor lost to intermediate underflow.

capability: Non-relativistic thermal-electron normalized momentum p_Te = sqrt(2T/mc^2), a dimensionless speed ratio rather than a velocity.
discovery.model: Independent closed-form definition, not a fit; dangerous intermediates are evaluated at high precision beyond binary64, with no automatic unit conversion.
discovery.geometry: Not applicable; scalar algebraic evaluation with no spatial axis.
discovery.boundary: The positive temperature-to-rest-energy ratio may underflow before the square root; the fallback preserves a representable positive root, and only a final value outside the binary64 range is rejected.

identity.relation: the thermal-electron normalized momentum p_Te as a function of the electron temperature and the electron rest energy
identity.definition: Returns the dimensionless non-relativistic thermal speed ratio sqrt(2*temperature_kev/restmkev). The ordinary region retains the original binary64 evaluation order; when an intermediate value overflows or becomes subnormal, the exact input floats are evaluated with 100-digit Decimal and the final result is rounded to binary64.
identity.model: an independent closed-form definition, not a fit; beyond ordinary binary64 arithmetic, dangerous intermediates are evaluated at high precision, with no automatic unit conversion
identity.geometry: not applicable; a scalar algebraic evaluation
identity.boundary: the ratio of positive temperature to rest energy may underflow before the square root; the fallback evaluation preserves a representable positive root, and only a final value outside the binary64 range is rejected
assumptions: both inputs are energies in the same unit; the supplied keV numbers are not converted. The non-relativistic relation provides no relativistic correction.

the two leaf entries are independent. A thermal speed ratio must not be passed as vnorm; the direct composition divides by c twice, so the caller must first multiply it by the speed of light to recover a velocity.
the ordinary region retains the original floating-point operation order; bit-for-bit agreement with the erroneous earlier operation at dangerous extremes is not promised.
shapes and finite inputs are checked first; the existing float() behavior for convertible non-real values is preserved, without adding physical meaning.

inputs.name: temperature_kev
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive, and scalar-shaped: a list, a tuple or an array with one or more dimensions is rejected by parameter name rather than converted. No upper bound is imposed; a finite value so large that the closed form is not representable is accepted by this constraint and rejected by the runtime representability check.

inputs.name: restmkev
inputs.description: Electron rest energy, in keV; 511.0 for an electron.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive, and scalar-shaped. The value is the caller's: this asset states no rest energy of its own and performs no unit conversion.

outputs.name: p_te
outputs.description: The thermal-electron normalized momentum sqrt(2*T/mc^2), dimensionless, a speed in units of c.
outputs.constraints: a Python float, finally finite and positive; not a velocity in cm/s. Intermediate floating-point overflow must not be misread as final closed-form non-representability

preconditions: The caller wants the non-relativistic thermal speed ratio sqrt(2T/mc^2) of an electron, or of a species whose rest energy the caller supplies in keV.
Both arguments are energies in the same unit, so the result is dimensionless.
supported: ordinary inputs retain the original scientific relation and double-precision operation order
dangerous intermediates use a Decimal fallback evaluated from the exact input floats; the input domain is not narrowed and verification tolerances are not relaxed
inputs with an invalid shape or a violated finiteness or sign contract are rejected by parameter name; final overflow is rejected and no partial result is returned
excluded: Composition with scirel.collisions.normalized-momentum: the two leaves are dimensionally incompatible and the direct composition divides by c twice, so it is not provided.
Any relativistic correction to the thermal speed ratio.
Any statement of the electron rest energy, of the speed of light, or of any other physical constant; every constant is the caller's.
Any unit conversion, including the conversion of the returned ratio to a velocity.
The four Coulomb-log mappings of the same family: they are different relations and are not published with these two leaves.
a final result outside the binary64 representable range is rejected; an overflowing intermediate result is not itself excluded

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when temperature_kev or restmkev is not scalar-shaped, or when either is not finite and strictly positive, with a message naming the offending parameter.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: raises ValueError only when the final value is still non-finite after the fallback computation. Intermediate product or quotient overflow, underflow or subnormal precision loss triggers the high-precision fallback rather than directly rejecting the input.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this operator has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no value.

example.description: demonstrate the retained ordinary relation together with the final result after correcting extreme intermediates
example.code:
from scirel.collisions import thermal_electron_momentum
import math
p = thermal_electron_momentum(temperature_kev=250., restmkev=511.)
assert p == 0.9891782353111633
large = thermal_electron_momentum(temperature_kev=1e308, restmkev=511.)
assert math.isfinite(large) and large > 1e152
tiny = thermal_electron_momentum(temperature_kev=1e-300, restmkev=1e300)
assert tiny > 0
print(p, large, tiny)
example.expected: the ordinary value 0.9891782353111633; the dangerous large value is about 6.256112470898544e152 and the tiny value about 1.414213562373095e-300, all finite

scope: the ordinary-domain numeric assertions, effective tolerances, input shapes and error messages are retained; ordinary results are bit-identical
of the 13 added extreme-value checks, 7 failed before the correction; they cover false rejection of finite large values, intermediate underflow to zero and sign preservation

independent 200-digit Decimal evaluation and genuine non-finite final-value rejection exercise the new behavior; the earlier rejection assertion for the thermal input 1e308/511 was empirically corrected and now supersedes the earlier record
the earlier external comparison is outside this contract's evidence scope; this contract binds only the two definitions and their independent scientific contracts
verification.evidence_ceiling: finite independent extreme-value and ordinary closed-form tests support the two definitions and their shape and representability contract; they do not establish arbitrary collision models, caller constants or units, or relativistic validity. The dangerous region uses 100-digit Decimal while outputs remain binary64; arbitrary-precision results are not claimed
known_limitations: no automatic unit check or conversion exists; using a thermal speed ratio directly as a velocity divides by the speed of light twice
the physical applicability domain remains the caller's responsibility; at extremely high temperature the non-relativistic ratio is only a definition, not a relativistic velocity
final binary64 rounding and underflow of genuinely tiny grid results to zero retain floating-point meaning and do not mean the physical quantity is exactly zero
